Verdict

The cycle is rolling from memory to the grid; compute and cloud have not turned

Three of the ten indicators are past their momentum peak (Alphabet backlog, Eaton orders, Micron DRAM pricing) and two are at it now (Eaton revenue, GE Vernova orders). Micron revenue is the only series with a high-probability level peak inside two years.

Memory turns first

Micron's DRAM price growth slowed to +19% QoQ in fiscal Q4 from +62% in fiscal Q3. Management expects price increases to moderate while conditions stay tight through 2028.  [1] New Micron supply starts with Idaho ID1 wafer output in mid-calendar 2027 and Tongluo shipments in mid-2027, with HBM packaging output in Singapore in early 2027.  [2] The cycle model places the trailing-revenue peak in 3Q27.

Grid order momentum has peaked

Eaton reported record orders up 41% on a rolling 12-month basis, with book-to-bill at 1.3.  [3] On a trailing basis, Eaton order growth eased to +29.5% from +34.2% the quarter before. GE Vernova Electrification orders rose 66% YoY to about $6.3B, roughly 1.7x revenue.  [4] Backlogs are still growing, so revenue keeps accelerating through 2H26.

Compute and cloud still accelerating

Google Cloud backlog rose by more than $50B sequentially to $514B.  [5] Net additions to Alphabet's total RPO fell from about $225B in 1Q26 to about $52B in 2Q26, the first deceleration in its order book. NVIDIA cites a cloud-industry backlog above $2T and top-five hyperscaler capex of nearly $800B in 2026 and $1.3T in 2027.  [6] NVIDIA's own purchase commitments tripled QoQ to $366B, so its supply chain is still being sized for growth.

Watch next

  • 28 Oct: GE Vernova and Alphabet 3Q prints. These test whether order momentum keeps rolling over.
  • 3 Nov: Eaton 3Q orders and book-to-bill.
  • About 25 Nov: NVIDIA fiscal Q3. About 23 Dec: Micron fiscal Q1, the first read on DRAM pricing after the slowdown.

Micron read

Revenue and HBM

Fiscal Q4 FY26 revenue was $54,229M [7] against $11,315M [8] a year earlier.

Cloud Memory revenue, the HBM-heavy unit, reached $16.3B in fiscal Q4 against $4.5B a year earlier.

Consensus has quarterly revenue at $83,614M [9] by fiscal Q4 FY28, which implies trailing growth slowing to about 18%.

Micron cites newly negotiated strategic customer agreement extensions and a very strong demand outlook through 2028, set against structural supply constraints.  [10]

Model read

Calibrated on Micron's own history, the cycle runs about 16 quarters. The base path turns trailing growth negative in 1Q28, which is more bearish than consensus.

NVIDIA (NVDA): revenue vs purchase commitments, YoY growth of trailing-twelve-month level

Actuals through 2Q26 (calendar). Dotted = consensus, dashed = cycle model. Left axis revenue, right axis purchase commitments.

NVIDIA read

Revenue and visibility

Fiscal Q2 FY27 revenue was $96,221M [11], up from $46,743M [12] a year earlier.

Vera Rubin production shipments began in August, and NVIDIA sizes its revenue opportunity at about $40B per gigawatt, against $25B for Blackwell.  [13]

AWS will deploy an additional 2 million NVIDIA GPUs through fiscal Q2 2029.  [6]

Consensus reaches $225,593M [14] in fiscal Q2 FY29, still implying trailing growth of about 55% at the end of the horizon.

Model read

Revenue momentum tops out in 3Q26, then growth decays toward the mid-20s by 2028. The base path shows no level peak, and the odds of one within two years are 32%. NVIDIA does not report orders. Its purchase commitments jumped from $119B to $366B in one quarter, too abrupt a step to project.

Alphabet (GOOGL): revenue vs total rpo, YoY growth of trailing-twelve-month level

Actuals through 2Q26 (calendar). Dotted = consensus, dashed = cycle model. Left axis revenue, right axis total rpo.

Alphabet read

Revenue and backlog

2Q26 revenue was $119,796M [15] against $96,428M [16] a year earlier.

Cloud revenue grew 82% on demand for AI infrastructure and AI solutions.  [17]

Alphabet expects to recognize just over 50% of the $514B Cloud backlog as revenue over the next 24 months.  [5]

Model read

RPO growth peaked at +406% YoY in 1Q26 and eased to +380% in 2Q26. Revenue momentum builds until about 4Q26, and consensus puts that peak at 2Q27. Revenue shows no level peak within four years. RPO projections are low confidence because the series is short and more than doubled in two quarters.

Eaton (ETN): revenue vs orders, YoY growth of trailing-twelve-month level

Actuals through 2Q26 (calendar). Dotted = consensus, dashed = cycle model. Left axis revenue, right axis orders.

Eaton read

Revenue and orders

2Q26 revenue was a record $8,531M [18] against $7,028M [19] a year earlier.

Eaton reported 21% total and 14% organic growth, total book-to-bill of 1.2, and robust data center orders.  [20]

Quarterly orders were $9.8B in 2Q26 after $10.5B in 1Q26. Backlog reached $24.1B, up 38% YoY.

Model read

Order momentum peaked in 1Q26, and revenue momentum is peaking now. Consensus has trailing revenue growth settling near 10% in 2028. The model is more conservative because Eaton's long-run revenue growth history is in the low single digits.

GE Vernova (GEV): revenue vs orders, YoY growth of trailing-twelve-month level

Actuals through 2Q26 (calendar). Dotted = consensus, dashed = cycle model. Left axis revenue, right axis orders.

GE Vernova read

Revenue and orders

2Q26 revenue was $11,104M [21] against $9,111M [22] a year earlier.

Total orders were $24.2B in 2Q26, nearly double the $12.4B of 2Q25, and RPO reached $176B.

GE Vernova booked $2.7B of Electrification data center orders in 2Q, taking 1H26 above $5B, more than double full-year 2025.  [23]

First-half 2026 equipment orders were priced more than 20% above 4Q25 equipment orders.  [24]

Model read

Trailing order growth is +76% and still rising. GE Vernova's own record starts in 2023, so the model is calibrated on Eaton's order history, and it expects the momentum peak in 2Q26. 3Q26 orders would need to exceed about $23.7B, against $14.6B in 3Q25, for trailing growth to keep accelerating. The 28 Oct print will show whether they did.

Company-reported figures compiled in Canalyst operating models. Backlog, RPO and commitments are period-end balances; orders and revenue are quarterly flows.

Method

Variables

  • Revenue: reported quarterly revenue, extended with the consensus quarterly path for eight quarters.
  • Orders: reported orders for Eaton and GE Vernova; total RPO (mostly Google Cloud backlog) for Alphabet; purchase commitments for NVIDIA; DRAM price momentum for Micron.

Derivatives

  • The trend level is the trailing-twelve-month sum for flows and the period-end balance for stocks, which strips out seasonality and lumpy bookings.
  • Velocity (first derivative) is the YoY growth of that level. Acceleration (second derivative) is the quarterly change in velocity.
  • The local zero-derivative point is where acceleration crosses from positive to negative, so growth tops out. The global zero-derivative point is where the level itself stops rising and holds below that high for the next four quarters.

Forecast

  • Velocity is projected with a damped second-order cycle model fitted on each company's own history since 2013: Micron 49 quarters, NVIDIA 51, Alphabet 47, Eaton 47, Eaton orders 27.
  • GE Vernova, which has traded only since 2024, borrows Eaton's parameters.
  • 4,000 resampled paths give the odds and interquartile range of each peak date. Fitted cycle lengths are 16 quarters for Micron, 15 for NVIDIA, 13 for Alphabet and 18 for Eaton revenue.
  • The model reverts each company toward its own long-run growth. That is why it runs more bearish than consensus for the industrials and more bullish for NVIDIA.
What is missing to define the problem fully
  • Orders at Micron and NVIDIA. Neither company discloses orders or backlog. The proxies used are DRAM price momentum and purchase commitments, and contracted HBM volumes or hyperscaler GPU order data would be stronger inputs.
  • The demand driver. Hyperscaler capex (Microsoft, Amazon, Meta, Oracle, Alphabet) funds all five order books. Adding it as a leading series would tie the model to the financing side of a bubble.
  • The financial side. Orders and revenue measure the real-economy cycle. A bubble call also needs valuation, debt-funded capex and customer-concentration measures, which are not in this model.
  • Alphabet scope. Total revenue is dominated by Search and YouTube. Google Cloud revenue would be a purer AI-services series if you prefer it.
  • Peak definition. This model uses trailing-twelve-month levels. A peak in the quarterly series would come about two quarters earlier.
  • GE Vernova history. With only 14 quarters of order data, its cycle parameters are borrowed and its peak dates carry the widest error.
